_doc: HMTc Category 19 (Laundry and Fabric-Contact Home Products) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-category.mjs. Method v2.0, government-limit default. THIRTEEN rows, one per taxonomy subcategory slug in data/taxonomy/hmtc-v2.json categories[] n=19. The hazard framing is residue left on fabric that is then worn in prolonged skin contact, plus the wash-water discharge pathway. NO sovereign government sets a heavy-metal maximum level for any product in this category; that is the finding of a full register survey, not a gap in the survey. The four toxic-panel cells (Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg) are disclosed read-across values from China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2, the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime in the register and already the read-across anchor of the live Category 12 standard for the identical logical move; nickel is a disclosed read-across from Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, the only regime in the register that sets a consumer-chemical nickel maximum, preserving the Korean instrument's own product-form split. Sn, Al, Cr and Cr-VI are held under mandatory analytical control with a published reference method, sampling unit, component sampling plan and escalation rule, and with companion sovereign limits disclosed where one governs a genuinely related form. iAs and MeHg are substantiated not-material determinations bounded by their total-element parents. China GB 14930.1-2022, the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register, is checked and excluded on scope: it governs food-cleaning and food-contact detergents, not laundry products, and a food-contact detergent limit does not automatically reach a fabric softener; its total-arsenic values are looser than the value adopted here in any event. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 (consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles, Pb/Cd/tAs/Cr-VI at 1 mg/kg after extraction) governs the FABRIC rather than the product applied to it and on a different basis; it is disclosed as a related but distinct scope and carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, never borrowed as a ceiling, and the row basis_guard makes borrowing it impossible in the compiler. Occurrence, eco-label and disclosure evidence (Green Seal GS-48/GS-51, EPA Safer Choice/DfE, EU Ecolabel for detergents, California SB 258, New York DEC disclosure BMP, and the routed product surveys) is used ONLY to establish that an analyte is material — and therefore that a not-material determination would be false — and to design the reference method and escalation rule. It never selects a number. Allowed provenance tags: regulatory-alignment, read-across, not-material, control, ratchet. STAFF / HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19 firewall).

_category.name: Laundry and Fabric-Contact Home Products
_category.anchor: data/taxonomy/hmtc-v2.json categories[] n=19, thirteen subcategory slugs; exposure pathway 'Dermal (residue on fabric in prolonged skin contact)'. The taxonomy's regulatory_anchors field names Green Seal GS-48 scope and EPA Safer Choice laundry product types; those are SCOPING anchors that define what belongs in the category, not sources of numeric limits, and neither sets a heavy-metal maximum level.
_category.basis_family: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis). Never a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed basis, never the textile homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis of the EU consumer-textile restriction, never an article migration or leachate basis, and never a percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restriction. Every row carries a basis_guard that enforces this in the compiler.
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; no sovereign sets a contaminant maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, so each toxic-panel cell is a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum level in the product's native as-sold content basis, and each remaining unregulated cell is a control with a published method and escalation rule; never occurrence-derived)
_category.method_note: No sovereign government sets a heavy-metal maximum level for a laundry or fabric-care product. The regimes that actually govern this sector — Green Seal GS-48 and GS-51 for laundry care products, the EPA Safer Choice programme and its Design for the Environment standard, the EU Ecolabel for detergents and cleaning products (Commission Decisions (EU) 2017/1214 to 2017/1219 and the 2024 user manual, with the JRC 2025 revision in progress), California SB 258 (the Cleaning Product Right to Know Act) and the New York DEC cleansing-product disclosure best-management practice — are eco-label, ingredient-disclosure and biodegradability regimes. They name lead, cadmium, total arsenic, total mercury, hexavalent chromium and nickel as substances of concern for laundry care and set NO numeric contaminant ceiling in the product, so they establish materiality and supply no number. China GB 14930.1-2022 is the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; its scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, so it does not reach a laundry detergent and still less a fabric softener, and its total-arsenic ceilings of 3.0 and 5.0 mg/kg are looser than the value adopted here in any event. The toxic panel is therefore read across from the nearest applicable coherent sovereign consumer-chemical regime in the same basis. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; ASEAN, Health Canada and BVL are guidance), and it is already the read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. Reading a cosmetic ceiling across to a fabric-care product is directionally conservative for the rinse-off rows, where the product is diluted in wash water and rinsed rather than applied neat to skin, and directly analogous for the leave-on rows, where the product is deliberately deposited on a textile that is then worn against skin; the sovereign instruments write no rinse-off/leave-on split for these analytes, so none is invented here and the exposure difference is disclosed in each row's scope note instead. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. The Germany BVL 2017 values that the audit scan surfaces as stricter are orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, carried in the register with status 'guidance impurity limit' rather than as statutory maximum levels; Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable MAXIMUM LEVEL set by a credible sovereign government, so a guidance orientation value is not selectable as an anchor. The same reasoning excludes the Health Canada cosmetic impurity limits and the ASEAN, Malaysia and Singapore guidance values. Occurrence, eco-label and disclosure evidence is used only to establish materiality — a not-material determination contradicted by a measurement in the routed corpus would be false and would fail the substantiation gate — and to design each control's reference method and escalation rule. It never selects a number.
_category.credible_note: The default credible-regulator set is widened by CN, KR and DE, and each addition is a recorded governance ruling rather than a convenience. CN: the NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics is a mandatory national standard and is already the read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move, and GB 14930.1-2022 is China's sovereign detergent-hygiene standard, checked here and excluded on scope. KR: MFDS Notice 2025-63 is a statutory cosmetics safety standard and supplies the only sovereign consumer-chemical NICKEL maximum in the register, which matters because nickel is the sensitising analyte this category's dermal pathway is built around. DE: the BVL 2017 'technically avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics' values are admitted to the audit scan deliberately, so that they SURFACE as stricter alternatives and are dispositioned on the record rather than quietly excluded; they are orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, carried in the register with status 'guidance impurity limit', and Method v2.0 selects among MAXIMUM LEVELS, so they are not selectable as anchors. That reasoning is recorded rather than hidden, and it is in tension with the live Category 15 (Feminine Care) standard, which does use a BVL row as a numeric read-across anchor; the inconsistency is flagged for governance and is not resolved inside this category.

laundry-detergents.name: Laundry detergents (liquid, powder, pods/sheets, delicates)
laundry-detergents.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis, mg/kg of product)
laundry-detergents.scope_note: Anionic and non-ionic surfactants, sodium carbonate and silicate alkalinity, sodium aluminosilicate (zeolite A) or phosphate builders, enzymes and optical brighteners, with a sodium percarbonate or perborate bleach system in many powders; unit-dose formats add a polyvinyl-alcohol film and sheet formats a nonwoven or cast-film substrate. The product is diluted in wash water and rinsed, so the dermal pathway is residual carryover deposited on fabric that is then worn in prolonged skin contact, together with the wash-water discharge pathway. Boundary rules for this category: the product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying or treatment; a carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery; and dryer sheets route to the fabric-softener row. No sovereign contaminant maximum exists for this product form. The four toxic-panel cells and the nickel cell are disclosed read-across values from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum levels in this row's native basis; the remaining unregulated cells are held under mandatory analytical control with a published method and escalation rule; and the two speciation cells are bounded by their total-element parents. No cell is occurrence-derived.
laundry-detergents.cross_reference: Hand dish soaps, automatic dishwasher detergents and hard-surface cleaners route to Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing); a detergent marketed for cleaning food or food-contact articles routes to the food-contact-cleaning rows of that category and is governed by China GB 14930.1-2022 rather than by this row.
laundry-detergents.audit_exclude_scope: ^toothpaste$|tattooing|permanent make-up|carbon black|colouring agent|colour additive|color additive|modeling clay|clay as a raw material
laundry-detergents.basis_guard: cosmetic product|finished cosmetic as sold|marketed cosmetic product|cosmetic colourant impurity
laundry-detergents.basis_guard_note: Every numeric cell on this row is a disclosed read-across from a sovereign maximum level set on a FINISHED CONSUMER-CHEMICAL PRODUCT expressed as total content of the product as placed on the market. The guard admits only that basis family (80 of the register's 2,993 rows as built) and therefore blocks, at compile time, the four basis conflations that would otherwise be available and would each be indefensible: a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed food maximum level; the EU consumer-textile restriction, which is a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis on the FABRIC rather than a content basis on the product applied to it; article migration and soluble-migration limits (EU Directive 2009/48/EC toys, jewellery and school-article rules); and percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restrictions (EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23 and 47, EU RoHS, and the tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis of entry 75). Those instruments are named and dispositioned in the cell substantiations and, where they govern a genuinely related form, are carried as companion limits on the control cells; none of them can anchor a number here.

Pb.basis_label: total lead content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)

read_across.label: disclosed read-across from China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (10 mg/kg lead in a finished consumer-chemical product), the nearest applicable sovereign maximum level on a finished consumer-chemical product in this row's native basis

China GB 14930.1-2022 does not reach this product form and carries no lead row in any event (its grouped heavy-metals line is expressed as combined heavy metals calculated as lead and is not loaded as a lead limit). The Germany BVL 2017 values that the audit scan surfaces as stricter are orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, carried in the register with status 'guidance impurity limit' rather than as statutory maximum levels; Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable MAXIMUM LEVEL set by a credible sovereign government, so a guidance orientation value is not selectable as an anchor. The same reasoning excludes the Health Canada cosmetic impurity limits and the ASEAN, Malaysia and Singapore guidance values. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Lead is measured in this product class in the routed corpus, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. Complete disposition of the stricter rows the compiler's audit safety-net surfaces for this row, none of which is adopted. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, register status 'guidance impurity limit', not statutory maximum levels, and therefore not selectable under Method v2.0. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so the list above is complete and nothing was excluded to make it shorter. Verification method: total lead by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the wash-active formulation and, for unit-dose and sheet formats, the polyvinyl-alcohol film or the sheet substrate, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. A lot at or above the published ceiling fails; a lot inside the ceiling but outside the running per-row control band is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back.

control.rationale: No sovereign sets a total- or inorganic-tin contaminant maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Every consumer-chemical regime in the register omits tin: China NMPA 2015 Table 2 covers lead, arsenic, mercury and cadmium; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 covers lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic and mercury; Germany BVL 2017 covers lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic and antimony; Health Canada covers the same five; and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 covers lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI). Every sovereign tin maximum in the register is a canned-food tinplate migration limit, and that pathway does not exist in a laundry product, so those values are inapplicable on both scope and basis. One sovereign instrument does reach this product form, but for a different species: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts dibutyltin compounds in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, and dioctyltin compounds in textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, to 0.1 per cent tin by weight (1000 mg/kg). That is a deliberate-use organotin restriction three orders of magnitude above any plausible contamination level, not a total-tin contaminant maximum; publishing it as this row's tin ceiling would substitute a species limit for a total-element cell, which the method forbids, and would advertise a firm limit no product could breach. The cell is therefore held under mandatory analytical control with no invented ceiling. It is deliberately NOT declared not-material: organotin compounds have a documented history as biocides and stabilisers in textile finishes, which is why entry 20 names skin-contact textiles at all, so an absence-of-pathway assertion would be rebuttable on this category's own facts.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total tin on every lot by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the wash-active formulation and, for unit-dose and sheet formats, the polyvinyl-alcohol film or the sheet substrate, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. Reflex organotin speciation (mono-, di- and tributyltin and dioctyltin by GC-ICP-MS or LC-MS/MS after derivatisation) on any total-tin result above the method reporting limit. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. Any organotin detection is additionally escalated as a regulatory matter and verified against the EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 ceiling of 0.1 per cent tin by weight, which is a compliance hard stop and not a certification band; a lot that breaches it cannot be certified at any status.

Percent-level aluminium is the expected condition on this row. The cell is a formulation-verification screen: it is not declared not-material, because aluminium is genuinely present and is reported on the panel, and it carries no invented ceiling, because no sovereign supplies one.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run, reported by ICP-OES where the expected concentration is percent-level and by ICP-MS otherwise; the declared aluminosilicate or aluminium-salt ingredient loading is recorded alongside every result. control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. The register's non-dietary total-chromium values are toy and school-article limits (Mexico NOM-252-SSA1-2011, China GB 21027-2020, the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations) and food gelatin limits; none reaches this product form and several are a soluble-migration basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Total chromium is carried as a SCREEN rather than as a health ceiling, in the same way the method treats total chromium generally: the total-element result is dominated by benign trivalent chromium from pigments, mineral feedstocks and stainless process equipment, and the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which is dispositioned on its own cell. Total chromium is measured in consumer cleaning and household hygienic products in the routed corpus (ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products, and for the detergent rows abulude2007-soaps-detergents-akure-nigeria and iwegbue2019-household-hygienic-products-nigeria), so the cell is material and cannot be declared not material.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable in this row's basis. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. laundry-detergent-boosters-additives.name: Laundry detergent boosters/additives
laundry-detergent-boosters-additives.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis, mg/kg of product)
laundry-detergent-boosters-additives.scope_note: Mined and refined mineral concentrates — sodium borate, sodium carbonate (soda ash), sodium sulfate, sodium percarbonate, and zeolite or phosphate water softeners — together with enzyme, surfactant and chelant boosters. The product is dosed into wash water alongside a detergent and rinsed; the dermal pathway is residual carryover on fabric worn in prolonged skin contact, plus the wash-water discharge pathway. This row is the most mineral-intensive in the category: borate, soda ash, sulfate and percarbonate are mined or mineral-derived feedstocks, and geogenic lead, cadmium and arsenic carried through from the ore body is the dominant contamination pathway rather than process contact. Boundary rules for this category: the product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying or treatment; a carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery; and dryer sheets route to the fabric-softener row. No sovereign contaminant maximum exists for this product form. The four toxic-panel cells and the nickel cell are disclosed read-across values from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum levels in this row's native basis; the remaining unregulated cells are held under mandatory analytical control with a published method and escalation rule; and the two speciation cells are bounded by their total-element parents. No cell is occurrence-derived.
laundry-detergent-boosters-additives.audit_exclude_scope: ^toothpaste$|tattooing|permanent make-up|carbon black|colouring agent|colour additive|color additive|modeling clay|clay as a raw material
laundry-detergent-boosters-additives.basis_guard: cosmetic product|finished cosmetic as sold|marketed cosmetic product|cosmetic colourant impurity
laundry-detergent-boosters-additives.basis_guard_note: Every numeric cell on this row is a disclosed read-across from a sovereign maximum level set on a FINISHED CONSUMER-CHEMICAL PRODUCT expressed as total content of the product as placed on the market. The guard admits only that basis family (80 of the register's 2,993 rows as built) and therefore blocks, at compile time, the four basis conflations that would otherwise be available and would each be indefensible: a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed food maximum level; the EU consumer-textile restriction, which is a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis on the FABRIC rather than a content basis on the product applied to it; article migration and soluble-migration limits (EU Directive 2009/48/EC toys, jewellery and school-article rules); and percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restrictions (EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23 and 47, EU RoHS, and the tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis of entry 75). Those instruments are named and dispositioned in the cell substantiations and, where they govern a genuinely related form, are carried as companion limits on the control cells; none of them can anchor a number here.

control.rationale: No sovereign sets a total- or inorganic-tin contaminant maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Every consumer-chemical regime in the register omits tin: China NMPA 2015 Table 2 covers lead, arsenic, mercury and cadmium; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 covers lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic and mercury; Germany BVL 2017 covers lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic and antimony; Health Canada covers the same five; and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 covers lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI). Every sovereign tin maximum in the register is a canned-food tinplate migration limit, and that pathway does not exist in a laundry product, so those values are inapplicable on both scope and basis. One sovereign instrument does reach this product form, but for a different species: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts dibutyltin compounds in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, and dioctyltin compounds in textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, to 0.1 per cent tin by weight (1000 mg/kg). That is a deliberate-use organotin restriction three orders of magnitude above any plausible contamination level, not a total-tin contaminant maximum; publishing it as this row's tin ceiling would substitute a species limit for a total-element cell, which the method forbids, and would advertise a firm limit no product could breach. The cell is therefore held under mandatory analytical control with no invented ceiling. It is deliberately NOT declared not-material: organotin compounds have a documented history as biocides and stabilisers in textile finishes, which is why entry 20 names skin-contact textiles at all, so an absence-of-pathway assertion would be rebuttable on this category's own facts.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total tin on every lot by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the mineral or powder concentrate and, for unit-dose, tablet or sachet formats, the film, coating or wrapper, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. Reflex organotin speciation (mono-, di- and tributyltin and dioctyltin by GC-ICP-MS or LC-MS/MS after derivatisation) on any total-tin result above the method reporting limit. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. Any organotin detection is additionally escalated as a regulatory matter and verified against the EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 ceiling of 0.1 per cent tin by weight, which is a compliance hard stop and not a certification band; a lot that breaches it cannot be certified at any status.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium maximum for any consumer-chemical product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China NMPA 2015 Table 2, Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, the ASEAN Annex, China GB 14930.1-2022 and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 all omit aluminium. The only non-dietary aluminium values in the register are the EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety limits, which are migration limits on an accessible toy material rather than content limits on a consumer chemical; this row's basis_guard blocks them from anchoring the cell. Aluminium is in any case a FUNCTIONAL INGREDIENT rather than a trace contaminant across much of this category: sodium aluminosilicate (zeolite A) is the standard phosphate-replacement builder in laundry powders and unit-dose formulations, and aluminium salts appear as processing aids and opacifiers, so an aluminium result on this row reports formulation design and not contamination. Percent-level aluminium is the expected condition on this row. The cell is a formulation-verification screen: it is not declared not-material, because aluminium is genuinely present and is reported on the panel, and it carries no invented ceiling, because no sovereign supplies one.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable in this row's basis. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Hexavalent chromium is expressly NOT declared not material in this category, and the method-artifact reasoning that supports a not-material determination for cooked foods does not transfer: the reducing, organic-rich, wet matrix that converts Cr(VI) to Cr(III) in a cooked food is absent here, and several rows in this category are deliberately oxidising and alkaline — hypochlorite, sodium percarbonate, sodium perborate, persulfate and peracid whitening chemistry, and oxygen boosters — which are conditions under which Cr(VI) is stable. Cr(VI) is named as a substance of concern for laundry care by greenseal2020-gs51-laundry-care-products, epa2024-safer-choice-standard-dfe and nydec2020-cleansing-product-disclosure-bmp, and is measured in consumer products in ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler; for this analyte that downstream fabric ceiling is 1 mg/kg, and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 sets 3 mg/kg in skin-contact leather articles. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Any hexavalent-chromium detection is escalated for formulation review, oxidiser and pigment trace-back, and a residue-transfer assessment against the EU consumer-textile ceiling of 1 mg/kg Cr(VI) in the treated fabric, which is a regulatory hard stop on the article and not a certification band.

pre-treaters-stain-removers.name: Pre-treaters (spray/gel/stick) and stand-alone stain/spot removers
pre-treaters-stain-removers.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis, mg/kg of product)
pre-treaters-stain-removers.scope_note: Concentrated surfactant, solvent, enzyme and chelant systems, sometimes with oxidising or reducing bleach chemistry and sometimes pigmented, applied undiluted to the fabric and left in contact for minutes to hours before washing. The product is applied neat to the textile and dwells there before the wash, so the deposited dose per unit fabric area is the highest of any rinse-off row in this category even though a wash cycle follows. Boundary rules for this category: the product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying or treatment; a carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery; and dryer sheets route to the fabric-softener row. No sovereign contaminant maximum exists for this product form. The four toxic-panel cells and the nickel cell are disclosed read-across values from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum levels in this row's native basis; the remaining unregulated cells are held under mandatory analytical control with a published method and escalation rule; and the two speciation cells are bounded by their total-element parents. No cell is occurrence-derived.
pre-treaters-stain-removers.cross_reference: A carpet or hard-surface spot cleaner routes to Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing); a spot treatment specifically marketed as a fabric-care product for upholstery routes here, per the Category 19 boundary rules.
pre-treaters-stain-removers.audit_exclude_scope: ^toothpaste$|tattooing|permanent make-up|carbon black|colouring agent|colour additive|color additive|modeling clay|clay as a raw material
pre-treaters-stain-removers.basis_guard: cosmetic product|finished cosmetic as sold|marketed cosmetic product|cosmetic colourant impurity
pre-treaters-stain-removers.basis_guard_note: Every numeric cell on this row is a disclosed read-across from a sovereign maximum level set on a FINISHED CONSUMER-CHEMICAL PRODUCT expressed as total content of the product as placed on the market. The guard admits only that basis family (80 of the register's 2,993 rows as built) and therefore blocks, at compile time, the four basis conflations that would otherwise be available and would each be indefensible: a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed food maximum level; the EU consumer-textile restriction, which is a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis on the FABRIC rather than a content basis on the product applied to it; article migration and soluble-migration limits (EU Directive 2009/48/EC toys, jewellery and school-article rules); and percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restrictions (EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23 and 47, EU RoHS, and the tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis of entry 75). Those instruments are named and dispositioned in the cell substantiations and, where they govern a genuinely related form, are carried as companion limits on the control cells; none of them can anchor a number here.

(1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, register status 'guidance impurity limit', not statutory maximum levels, and therefore not selectable under Method v2.0. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. Verification method: total lead by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. A lot at or above the published ceiling fails; a lot inside the ceiling but outside the running per-row control band is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back.

A food-contact detergent limit does not automatically reach a fabric-care product, and nothing turns on the exclusion in any case because both GB 14930.1 values are LOOSER than the 2 mg/kg adopted here. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; ASEAN, Health Canada and BVL are guidance), and it is already the read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. The Germany BVL 2017 values that the audit scan surfaces as stricter are orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, carried in the register with status 'guidance impurity limit' rather than as statutory maximum levels; Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable MAXIMUM LEVEL set by a credible sovereign government, so a guidance orientation value is not selectable as an anchor. The same reasoning excludes the Health Canada cosmetic impurity limits and the ASEAN, Malaysia and Singapore guidance values. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Arsenic is named for this product class by the sector regimes and measured in household hygienic and cleaning products in the routed corpus, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, register status 'guidance impurity limit', not statutory maximum levels, and therefore not selectable under Method v2.0. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so the list above is complete and nothing was excluded to make it shorter. Verification method: total total arsenic by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. not_material.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic and a species of it (iAs <= tAs). The inorganic fraction is therefore governed by, and bounded by, the total-arsenic ceiling published on the tAs cell of this row. The determination is a governance statement about which cell carries the ceiling, not an assertion that inorganic arsenic is absent, and it is rebuttable: the only routed inorganic-arsenic measurement anywhere in this category's evidence base is zhang2026-cotton-arsenic-amf-calcium, which speciates inorganic arsenic in COTTON FIBRE as a soil-uptake pathway in the textile substrate, not as a contaminant of a product applied to the textile, so it does not rebut this determination for the product itself.
not_material.reference_method: Reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on the digest of the product as placed on the market, triggered whenever total arsenic exceeds one half of the published total-arsenic ceiling, whenever an arsenic-bearing mineral feedstock is declared, or whenever an agricultural (starch, cellulose or plant-derived surfactant) feedstock is declared. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the concentrate and, for stick and roll-on formats, the applicator wick or pad; trigger-spray and aerosol hardware in the product-contact path is sampled separately. Escalation: a speciated inorganic-arsenic result is dispositioned against the total-arsenic ceiling under ALARA with raw-material trace-back to the declared feedstock.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for a laundry, fabric-care, detergent or cosmetic product; every applicable consumer-chemical instrument regulates total arsenic. Inorganic arsenic is a species of and bounded by total arsenic (iAs <= tAs) and is governed through the tAs cell of this row, which carries a published ceiling.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a species of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food webs and concentrated by dietary bioaccumulation in fish muscle. control.rationale: No sovereign sets a total- or inorganic-tin contaminant maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Every consumer-chemical regime in the register omits tin: China NMPA 2015 Table 2 covers lead, arsenic, mercury and cadmium; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 covers lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic and mercury; Germany BVL 2017 covers lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic and antimony; Health Canada covers the same five; and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 covers lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI). Every sovereign tin maximum in the register is a canned-food tinplate migration limit, and that pathway does not exist in a laundry product, so those values are inapplicable on both scope and basis. One sovereign instrument does reach this product form, but for a different species: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts dibutyltin compounds in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, and dioctyltin compounds in textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, to 0.1 per cent tin by weight (1000 mg/kg). That is a deliberate-use organotin restriction three orders of magnitude above any plausible contamination level, not a total-tin contaminant maximum; publishing it as this row's tin ceiling would substitute a species limit for a total-element cell, which the method forbids, and would advertise a firm limit no product could breach. The cell is therefore held under mandatory analytical control with no invented ceiling. It is deliberately NOT declared not-material: organotin compounds have a documented history as biocides and stabilisers in textile finishes, which is why entry 20 names skin-contact textiles at all, so an absence-of-pathway assertion would be rebuttable on this category's own facts.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total tin on every lot by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the concentrate and, for stick and roll-on formats, the applicator wick or pad; trigger-spray and aerosol hardware in the product-contact path is sampled separately. Reflex organotin speciation (mono-, di- and tributyltin and dioctyltin by GC-ICP-MS or LC-MS/MS after derivatisation) on any total-tin result above the method reporting limit. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. Any organotin detection is additionally escalated as a regulatory matter and verified against the EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 ceiling of 0.1 per cent tin by weight, which is a compliance hard stop and not a certification band; a lot that breaches it cannot be certified at any status.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium maximum for any consumer-chemical product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China NMPA 2015 Table 2, Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, the ASEAN Annex, China GB 14930.1-2022 and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 all omit aluminium. The only non-dietary aluminium values in the register are the EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety limits, which are migration limits on an accessible toy material rather than content limits on a consumer chemical; this row's basis_guard blocks them from anchoring the cell. Aluminium is in any case a FUNCTIONAL INGREDIENT rather than a trace contaminant across much of this category: sodium aluminosilicate (zeolite A) is the standard phosphate-replacement builder in laundry powders and unit-dose formulations, and aluminium salts appear as processing aids and opacifiers, so an aluminium result on this row reports formulation design and not contamination. An aluminosilicate builder is not expected in this row's chemistry, so any percent-level aluminium result is itself the finding. The cell is a formulation-verification screen: it is not declared not-material, because aluminium is genuinely present and is reported on the panel, and it carries no invented ceiling, because no sovereign supplies one.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run, reported by ICP-OES where the expected concentration is percent-level and by ICP-MS otherwise; the declared aluminosilicate or aluminium-salt ingredient loading is recorded alongside every result. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the concentrate and, for stick and roll-on formats, the applicator wick or pad; trigger-spray and aerosol hardware in the product-contact path is sampled separately. Escalation: a result materially above the declared functional-ingredient expectation, or any aluminium above the method reporting limit in a formulation that declares no aluminium-bearing ingredient, triggers ingredient and raw-material review, mineral-feedstock trace-back and supplier corrective action before the lot is released under certification. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable in this row's basis. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Hexavalent chromium is expressly NOT declared not material in this category, and the method-artifact reasoning that supports a not-material determination for cooked foods does not transfer: the reducing, organic-rich, wet matrix that converts Cr(VI) to Cr(III) in a cooked food is absent here, and several rows in this category are deliberately oxidising and alkaline — hypochlorite, sodium percarbonate, sodium perborate, persulfate and peracid whitening chemistry, and oxygen boosters — which are conditions under which Cr(VI) is stable. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. bleaching-whitening-additives.name: Bleaching/whitening additives
bleaching-whitening-additives.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis, mg/kg of product)
bleaching-whitening-additives.scope_note: Sodium hypochlorite, sodium percarbonate, sodium perborate, persulfate and peracid whitening systems with optical brighteners, and in some products reducing sulfite or hydrosulfite chemistry. The product is dosed into wash water and rinsed; the dermal pathway is residual carryover on fabric worn in prolonged skin contact, plus the wash-water discharge pathway. Percarbonate, perborate and persulfate are mineral-derived oxidiser feedstocks, so geogenic carry-through is a live contamination pathway alongside process contact. Boundary rules for this category: the product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying or treatment; a carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery; and dryer sheets route to the fabric-softener row. No sovereign contaminant maximum exists for this product form. The four toxic-panel cells and the nickel cell are disclosed read-across values from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum levels in this row's native basis; the remaining unregulated cells are held under mandatory analytical control with a published method and escalation rule; and the two speciation cells are bounded by their total-element parents. No cell is occurrence-derived.
bleaching-whitening-additives.cross_reference: A hypochlorite product marketed for hard-surface disinfection rather than for fabric whitening routes to Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing).
bleaching-whitening-additives.audit_exclude_scope: ^toothpaste$|tattooing|permanent make-up|carbon black|colouring agent|colour additive|color additive|modeling clay|clay as a raw material
bleaching-whitening-additives.basis_guard: cosmetic product|finished cosmetic as sold|marketed cosmetic product|cosmetic colourant impurity
bleaching-whitening-additives.basis_guard_note: Every numeric cell on this row is a disclosed read-across from a sovereign maximum level set on a FINISHED CONSUMER-CHEMICAL PRODUCT expressed as total content of the product as placed on the market. The guard admits only that basis family (80 of the register's 2,993 rows as built) and therefore blocks, at compile time, the four basis conflations that would otherwise be available and would each be indefensible: a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed food maximum level; the EU consumer-textile restriction, which is a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis on the FABRIC rather than a content basis on the product applied to it; article migration and soluble-migration limits (EU Directive 2009/48/EC toys, jewellery and school-article rules); and percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restrictions (EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23 and 47, EU RoHS, and the tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis of entry 75). Those instruments are named and dispositioned in the cell substantiations and, where they govern a genuinely related form, are carried as companion limits on the control cells; none of them can anchor a number here.

(1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, register status 'guidance impurity limit', not statutory maximum levels, and therefore not selectable under Method v2.0. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so the list above is complete and nothing was excluded to make it shorter. Verification method: total lead by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the bleaching concentrate and, for unit-dose or tablet formats, the film, coating or wrapper, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. A lot at or above the published ceiling fails; a lot inside the ceiling but outside the running per-row control band is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back.

Every sovereign tin maximum in the register is a canned-food tinplate migration limit, and that pathway does not exist in a laundry product, so those values are inapplicable on both scope and basis. One sovereign instrument does reach this product form, but for a different species: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts dibutyltin compounds in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, and dioctyltin compounds in textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, to 0.1 per cent tin by weight (1000 mg/kg). That is a deliberate-use organotin restriction three orders of magnitude above any plausible contamination level, not a total-tin contaminant maximum; publishing it as this row's tin ceiling would substitute a species limit for a total-element cell, which the method forbids, and would advertise a firm limit no product could breach. The cell is therefore held under mandatory analytical control with no invented ceiling. It is deliberately NOT declared not-material: organotin compounds have a documented history as biocides and stabilisers in textile finishes, which is why entry 20 names skin-contact textiles at all, so an absence-of-pathway assertion would be rebuttable on this category's own facts.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total tin on every lot by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium maximum for any consumer-chemical product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable in this row's basis. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Hexavalent chromium is expressly NOT declared not material in this category, and the method-artifact reasoning that supports a not-material determination for cooked foods does not transfer: the reducing, organic-rich, wet matrix that converts Cr(VI) to Cr(III) in a cooked food is absent here, and several rows in this category are deliberately oxidising and alkaline — hypochlorite, sodium percarbonate, sodium perborate, persulfate and peracid whitening chemistry, and oxygen boosters — which are conditions under which Cr(VI) is stable. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. fabric-softeners.name: Fabric softeners (liquids and sheets)
fabric-softeners.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis, mg/kg of product)
fabric-softeners.scope_note: Cationic esterquat and quaternary-ammonium softening actives, silicone emulsions, fatty alcohols, humectants and fragrance, delivered either as a rinse-added liquid or coated onto a nonwoven dryer sheet. This is a leave-on row: the product is designed to deposit and persist on the textile through drying and wear, so its residue is in prolonged, repeated skin contact and is not removed by a subsequent rinse. Dryer sheets route here per the Category 19 boundary rules. Boundary rules for this category: the product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying or treatment; a carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery; and dryer sheets route to the fabric-softener row. No sovereign contaminant maximum exists for this product form. The four toxic-panel cells and the nickel cell are disclosed read-across values from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum levels in this row's native basis; the remaining unregulated cells are held under mandatory analytical control with a published method and escalation rule; and the two speciation cells are bounded by their total-element parents. No cell is occurrence-derived.
fabric-softeners.audit_exclude_scope: ^toothpaste$|tattooing|permanent make-up|carbon black|colouring agent|colour additive|color additive|modeling clay|clay as a raw material
fabric-softeners.basis_guard: cosmetic product|finished cosmetic as sold|marketed cosmetic product|cosmetic colourant impurity
fabric-softeners.basis_guard_note: Every numeric cell on this row is a disclosed read-across from a sovereign maximum level set on a FINISHED CONSUMER-CHEMICAL PRODUCT expressed as total content of the product as placed on the market. The guard admits only that basis family (80 of the register's 2,993 rows as built) and therefore blocks, at compile time, the four basis conflations that would otherwise be available and would each be indefensible: a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed food maximum level; the EU consumer-textile restriction, which is a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis on the FABRIC rather than a content basis on the product applied to it; article migration and soluble-migration limits (EU Directive 2009/48/EC toys, jewellery and school-article rules); and percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restrictions (EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23 and 47, EU RoHS, and the tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis of entry 75). Those instruments are named and dispositioned in the cell substantiations and, where they govern a genuinely related form, are carried as companion limits on the control cells; none of them can anchor a number here.
