control.rationale: No sovereign sets a total- or inorganic-tin contaminant maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Every consumer-chemical regime in the register omits tin: China NMPA 2015 Table 2 covers lead, arsenic, mercury and cadmium; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 covers lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic and mercury; Germany BVL 2017 covers lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic and antimony; Health Canada covers the same five; and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 covers lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI). Every sovereign tin maximum in the register is a canned-food tinplate migration limit, and that pathway does not exist in a laundry product, so those values are inapplicable on both scope and basis. One sovereign instrument does reach this product form, but for a different species: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts dibutyltin compounds in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, and dioctyltin compounds in textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, to 0.1 per cent tin by weight (1000 mg/kg). That is a deliberate-use organotin restriction three orders of magnitude above any plausible contamination level, not a total-tin contaminant maximum; publishing it as this row's tin ceiling would substitute a species limit for a total-element cell, which the method forbids, and would advertise a firm limit no product could breach. The cell is therefore held under mandatory analytical control with no invented ceiling. It is deliberately NOT declared not-material: organotin compounds have a documented history as biocides and stabilisers in textile finishes, which is why entry 20 names skin-contact textiles at all, so an absence-of-pathway assertion would be rebuttable on this category's own facts.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total tin on every lot by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the concentrate or powder and, for unit-dose and sachet formats, the film or wrapper, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. Reflex organotin speciation (mono-, di- and tributyltin and dioctyltin by GC-ICP-MS or LC-MS/MS after derivatisation) on any total-tin result above the method reporting limit. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. Any organotin detection is additionally escalated as a regulatory matter and verified against the EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 ceiling of 0.1 per cent tin by weight, which is a compliance hard stop and not a certification band; a lot that breaches it cannot be certified at any status.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium maximum for any consumer-chemical product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China NMPA 2015 Table 2, Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, the ASEAN Annex, China GB 14930.1-2022 and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 all omit aluminium. The only non-dietary aluminium values in the register are the EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety limits, which are migration limits on an accessible toy material rather than content limits on a consumer chemical; this row's basis_guard blocks them from anchoring the cell. Aluminium is in any case a FUNCTIONAL INGREDIENT rather than a trace contaminant across much of this category: sodium aluminosilicate (zeolite A) is the standard phosphate-replacement builder in laundry powders and unit-dose formulations, and aluminium salts appear as processing aids and opacifiers, so an aluminium result on this row reports formulation design and not contamination. Percent-level aluminium is the expected condition on this row. The cell is a formulation-verification screen: it is not declared not-material, because aluminium is genuinely present and is reported on the panel, and it carries no invented ceiling, because no sovereign supplies one.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run, reported by ICP-OES where the expected concentration is percent-level and by ICP-MS otherwise; the declared aluminosilicate or aluminium-salt ingredient loading is recorded alongside every result. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the concentrate or powder and, for unit-dose and sachet formats, the film or wrapper, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. Escalation: a result materially above the declared functional-ingredient expectation, or any aluminium above the method reporting limit in a formulation that declares no aluminium-bearing ingredient, triggers ingredient and raw-material review, mineral-feedstock trace-back and supplier corrective action before the lot is released under certification. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. No consumer-chemical regime in the register sets a chromium row: China NMPA 2015 Table 2, Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, the ASEAN Annex and China GB 14930.1-2022 all omit it. The register's non-dietary total-chromium values are toy and school-article limits (Mexico NOM-252-SSA1-2011, China GB 21027-2020, the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations) and food gelatin limits; none reaches this product form and several are a soluble-migration basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Total chromium is carried as a SCREEN rather than as a health ceiling, in the same way the method treats total chromium generally: the total-element result is dominated by benign trivalent chromium from pigments, mineral feedstocks and stainless process equipment, and the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which is dispositioned on its own cell. Total chromium is measured in consumer cleaning and household hygienic products in the routed corpus (ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products, and for the detergent rows abulude2007-soaps-detergents-akure-nigeria and iwegbue2019-household-hygienic-products-nigeria), so the cell is material and cannot be declared not material.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present, which is the normal case on this row) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the concentrate or powder and, for unit-dose and sachet formats, the film or wrapper, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. The total-chromium result is the trigger for the hexavalent-chromium determination on the Cr-VI cell as well as a screen in its own right. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. An elevated total chromium additionally triggers the hexavalent-chromium determination, pigment and mineral-feedstock trace-back, and a process-equipment leaching assessment.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable in this row's basis. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Hexavalent chromium is expressly NOT declared not material in this category, and the method-artifact reasoning that supports a not-material determination for cooked foods does not transfer: the reducing, organic-rich, wet matrix that converts Cr(VI) to Cr(III) in a cooked food is absent here, and several rows in this category are deliberately oxidising and alkaline — hypochlorite, sodium percarbonate, sodium perborate, persulfate and peracid whitening chemistry, and oxygen boosters — which are conditions under which Cr(VI) is stable. Cr(VI) is named as a substance of concern for laundry care by greenseal2020-gs51-laundry-care-products, epa2024-safer-choice-standard-dfe and nydec2020-cleansing-product-disclosure-bmp, and is measured in consumer products in ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler; for this analyte that downstream fabric ceiling is 1 mg/kg, and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 sets 3 mg/kg in skin-contact leather articles. Those are real sovereign Cr(VI) ceilings one step downstream of this product, on the treated article rather than on the treatment, and they are carried as the constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile or leather to breach — not as this row's ceiling, which the basis_guard prevents in any case. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes.
control.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by alkaline digestion and ion chromatography with ICP-MS or post-column UV-Vis detection (US EPA 3060A with 7199, adapted and validated for this product matrix, with matrix-spike recovery reported on every run to demonstrate that the alkaline extraction has not itself oxidised trivalent chromium). Hexavalent-chromium determination is MANDATORY on any lot whose formulation is oxidising or alkaline (hypochlorite, percarbonate, perborate, persulfate or peracid chemistry, or a formulation pH at or above 10), which covers most powder and unit-dose variants on this row, and reflex otherwise. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the concentrate or powder and, for unit-dose and sachet formats, the film or wrapper, each sampled and tested as a distinct component. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. Any hexavalent-chromium detection is escalated for formulation review, oxidiser and pigment trace-back, and a residue-transfer assessment against the EU consumer-textile ceiling of 1 mg/kg Cr(VI) in the treated fabric, which is a regulatory hard stop on the article and not a certification band.

laundry-starch-sizing-fabric-finish.name: Laundry starch/sizing/fabric finish products
laundry-starch-sizing-fabric-finish.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis, mg/kg of product)
laundry-starch-sizing-fabric-finish.scope_note: Corn, wheat, rice or tapioca starch, polyvinyl acetate and polyvinyl alcohol sizing, silicone and wax finishes, delivered as an aerosol, a trigger spray or a dissolvable powder and usually heat-set with an iron. This is a leave-on row: the starch or sizing film is deliberately fixed onto the textile and worn against skin until the next wash. The starch base is an agricultural feedstock, so crop-uptake metals travel into the product with the raw material. Rice starch in particular is drawn from a recognised arsenic accumulator, which is why total arsenic and the reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation carry additional weight on this row and why the declared starch botanical origin is recorded with every arsenic result. Boundary rules for this category: the product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying or treatment; a carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery; and dryer sheets route to the fabric-softener row. No sovereign contaminant maximum exists for this product form. The four toxic-panel cells and the nickel cell are disclosed read-across values from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum levels in this row's native basis; the remaining unregulated cells are held under mandatory analytical control with a published method and escalation rule; and the two speciation cells are bounded by their total-element parents. No cell is occurrence-derived.
laundry-starch-sizing-fabric-finish.audit_exclude_scope: ^toothpaste$|tattooing|permanent make-up|carbon black|colouring agent|colour additive|color additive|modeling clay|clay as a raw material
laundry-starch-sizing-fabric-finish.basis_guard: cosmetic product|finished cosmetic as sold|marketed cosmetic product|cosmetic colourant impurity
laundry-starch-sizing-fabric-finish.basis_guard_note: Every numeric cell on this row is a disclosed read-across from a sovereign maximum level set on a FINISHED CONSUMER-CHEMICAL PRODUCT expressed as total content of the product as placed on the market. The guard admits only that basis family (80 of the register's 2,993 rows as built) and therefore blocks, at compile time, the four basis conflations that would otherwise be available and would each be indefensible: a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed food maximum level; the EU consumer-textile restriction, which is a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis on the FABRIC rather than a content basis on the product applied to it; article migration and soluble-migration limits (EU Directive 2009/48/EC toys, jewellery and school-article rules); and percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restrictions (EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23 and 47, EU RoHS, and the tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis of entry 75). Those instruments are named and dispositioned in the cell substantiations and, where they govern a genuinely related form, are carried as companion limits on the control cells; none of them can anchor a number here.

Pb.basis_label: total lead content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)

read_across.label: disclosed read-across from China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (10 mg/kg lead in a finished consumer-chemical product), the nearest applicable sovereign maximum level on a finished consumer-chemical product in this row's native basis
read_across.substantiation: No sovereign government sets a lead maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China GB 14930.1-2022 does not reach this product form and carries no lead row in any event (its grouped heavy-metals line is expressed as combined heavy metals calculated as lead and is not loaded as a lead limit). The sector regimes — Green Seal GS-48 and GS-51 for laundry care products, the EPA Safer Choice programme and its Design for the Environment standard, the EU Ecolabel for detergents and cleaning products (Commission Decisions (EU) 2017/1214 to 2017/1219 and the 2024 user manual, with the JRC 2025 revision in progress), California SB 258 (the Cleaning Product Right to Know Act) and the New York DEC cleansing-product disclosure best-management practice — name lead as a substance of concern for laundry care but set no numeric ceiling, so they establish materiality and supply no number. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; ASEAN, Health Canada and BVL are guidance), and it is already the read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. The Germany BVL 2017 values that the audit scan surfaces as stricter are orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, carried in the register with status 'guidance impurity limit' rather than as statutory maximum levels; Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable MAXIMUM LEVEL set by a credible sovereign government, so a guidance orientation value is not selectable as an anchor. The same reasoning excludes the Health Canada cosmetic impurity limits and the ASEAN, Malaysia and Singapore guidance values. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Lead is measured in this product class in the routed corpus, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. Complete disposition of the stricter rows the compiler's audit safety-net surfaces for this row, none of which is adopted. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, register status 'guidance impurity limit', not statutory maximum levels, and therefore not selectable under Method v2.0. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so the list above is complete and nothing was excluded to make it shorter. Verification method: total lead by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the starch or sizing concentrate and, for aerosol formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. A lot at or above the published ceiling fails; a lot inside the ceiling but outside the running per-row control band is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back.

Cd.basis_label: total cadmium content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)

read_across.label: disclosed read-across from China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (5 mg/kg cadmium in a finished consumer-chemical product), the nearest applicable sovereign maximum level on a finished consumer-chemical product in this row's native basis
read_across.substantiation: No sovereign government sets a cadmium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. not_material.reference_method: Reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on the digest of the product as placed on the market, triggered whenever total arsenic exceeds one half of the published total-arsenic ceiling, whenever an arsenic-bearing mineral feedstock is declared, or whenever an agricultural (starch, cellulose or plant-derived surfactant) feedstock is declared. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so the list above is complete and nothing was excluded to make it shorter. Verification method: total nickel by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the starch or sizing concentrate and, for aerosol formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. control.rationale: No sovereign sets a total- or inorganic-tin contaminant maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Every consumer-chemical regime in the register omits tin: China NMPA 2015 Table 2 covers lead, arsenic, mercury and cadmium; Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 covers lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic and mercury; Germany BVL 2017 covers lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic and antimony; Health Canada covers the same five; and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 covers lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI). Every sovereign tin maximum in the register is a canned-food tinplate migration limit, and that pathway does not exist in a laundry product, so those values are inapplicable on both scope and basis. One sovereign instrument does reach this product form, but for a different species: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 restricts dibutyltin compounds in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, and dioctyltin compounds in textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, to 0.1 per cent tin by weight (1000 mg/kg). That is a deliberate-use organotin restriction three orders of magnitude above any plausible contamination level, not a total-tin contaminant maximum; publishing it as this row's tin ceiling would substitute a species limit for a total-element cell, which the method forbids, and would advertise a firm limit no product could breach. The cell is therefore held under mandatory analytical control with no invented ceiling. It is deliberately NOT declared not-material: organotin compounds have a documented history as biocides and stabilisers in textile finishes, which is why entry 20 names skin-contact textiles at all, so an absence-of-pathway assertion would be rebuttable on this category's own facts.
control.reference_method: Mandatory total tin on every lot by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the starch or sizing concentrate and, for aerosol formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. Reflex organotin speciation (mono-, di- and tributyltin and dioctyltin by GC-ICP-MS or LC-MS/MS after derivatisation) on any total-tin result above the method reporting limit. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. Any organotin detection is additionally escalated as a regulatory matter and verified against the EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 ceiling of 0.1 per cent tin by weight, which is a compliance hard stop and not a certification band; a lot that breaches it cannot be certified at any status.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an aluminium maximum for any consumer-chemical product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. China NMPA 2015 Table 2, Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, the ASEAN Annex, China GB 14930.1-2022 and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 all omit aluminium. The only non-dietary aluminium values in the register are the EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety limits, which are migration limits on an accessible toy material rather than content limits on a consumer chemical; this row's basis_guard blocks them from anchoring the cell. Aluminium is in any case a FUNCTIONAL INGREDIENT rather than a trace contaminant across much of this category: sodium aluminosilicate (zeolite A) is the standard phosphate-replacement builder in laundry powders and unit-dose formulations, and aluminium salts appear as processing aids and opacifiers, so an aluminium result on this row reports formulation design and not contamination. An aluminosilicate builder is not expected in this row's chemistry, so any percent-level aluminium result is itself the finding. The cell is a formulation-verification screen: it is not declared not-material, because aluminium is genuinely present and is reported on the panel, and it carries no invented ceiling, because no sovereign supplies one.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run, reported by ICP-OES where the expected concentration is percent-level and by ICP-MS otherwise; the declared aluminosilicate or aluminium-salt ingredient loading is recorded alongside every result. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the starch or sizing concentrate and, for aerosol formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. Escalation: a result materially above the declared functional-ingredient expectation, or any aluminium above the method reporting limit in a formulation that declares no aluminium-bearing ingredient, triggers ingredient and raw-material review, mineral-feedstock trace-back and supplier corrective action before the lot is released under certification. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. No consumer-chemical regime in the register sets a chromium row: China NMPA 2015 Table 2, Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63, Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, the ASEAN Annex and China GB 14930.1-2022 all omit it. The register's non-dietary total-chromium values are toy and school-article limits (Mexico NOM-252-SSA1-2011, China GB 21027-2020, the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations) and food gelatin limits; none reaches this product form and several are a soluble-migration basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Total chromium is carried as a SCREEN rather than as a health ceiling, in the same way the method treats total chromium generally: the total-element result is dominated by benign trivalent chromium from pigments, mineral feedstocks and stainless process equipment, and the health-relevant species is hexavalent chromium, which is dispositioned on its own cell. Total chromium is measured in consumer cleaning and household hygienic products in the routed corpus (ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products, and for the detergent rows abulude2007-soaps-detergents-akure-nigeria and iwegbue2019-household-hygienic-products-nigeria), so the cell is material and cannot be declared not material.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the starch or sizing concentrate and, for aerosol formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. The total-chromium result is the trigger for the hexavalent-chromium determination on the Cr-VI cell as well as a screen in its own right. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. An elevated total chromium additionally triggers the hexavalent-chromium determination, pigment and mineral-feedstock trace-back, and a process-equipment leaching assessment.

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable in this row's basis. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. Hexavalent chromium is expressly NOT declared not material in this category, and the method-artifact reasoning that supports a not-material determination for cooked foods does not transfer: the reducing, organic-rich, wet matrix that converts Cr(VI) to Cr(III) in a cooked food is absent here, and several rows in this category are deliberately oxidising and alkaline — hypochlorite, sodium percarbonate, sodium perborate, persulfate and peracid whitening chemistry, and oxygen boosters — which are conditions under which Cr(VI) is stable. Cr(VI) is named as a substance of concern for laundry care by greenseal2020-gs51-laundry-care-products, epa2024-safer-choice-standard-dfe and nydec2020-cleansing-product-disclosure-bmp, and is measured in consumer products in ecetoc1992-tr045-ni-co-cr-consumer-products. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler; for this analyte that downstream fabric ceiling is 1 mg/kg, and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 sets 3 mg/kg in skin-contact leather articles. Those are real sovereign Cr(VI) ceilings one step downstream of this product, on the treated article rather than on the treatment, and they are carried as the constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile or leather to breach — not as this row's ceiling, which the basis_guard prevents in any case. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes.
control.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by alkaline digestion and ion chromatography with ICP-MS or post-column UV-Vis detection (US EPA 3060A with 7199, adapted and validated for this product matrix, with matrix-spike recovery reported on every run to demonstrate that the alkaline extraction has not itself oxidised trivalent chromium). Hexavalent-chromium determination is reflex: it is triggered by an elevated total-chromium screen, by a pigmented or mineral-bearing formulation, or by any oxidising or alkaline component. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the starch or sizing concentrate and, for aerosol formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. Because no sovereign ceiling exists for this cell, no pass/fail threshold is published. Every lot result is recorded against the running per-row control band (the trailing distribution of certified-lot results for this row and analyte). A result outside that band, or any first-time detection in a formulation whose declared ingredients supply no source for the analyte, triggers raw-material and process trace-back, supplier corrective action and re-test before the lot is released under certification, and the finding is carried into the annual review. Any hexavalent-chromium detection is escalated for formulation review, oxidiser and pigment trace-back, and a residue-transfer assessment against the EU consumer-textile ceiling of 1 mg/kg Cr(VI) in the treated fabric, which is a regulatory hard stop on the article and not a certification band.

fabric-protectants.name: Fabric protectants (excluding waterproofing/flame-retardant per GS-48 boundaries)
fabric-protectants.native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content of the finished product as placed on the market (as-sold consumer-chemical product-content basis, mg/kg of product)
fabric-protectants.scope_note: Fluoropolymer, silicone and dendrimer soil- and stain-repellent finishes, in some products combined with antimicrobial actives. This is a leave-on row and the most durable finish in the category: the protectant is designed to survive repeated wash cycles on upholstery and garments, so its residue is in prolonged, repeated skin contact over the life of the textile. Boundary rules for this category: the product must be intended to contact fabrics during washing, drying or treatment; a carpet cleaner is Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) unless it is specifically a fabric-care product for upholstery; and dryer sheets route to the fabric-softener row. No sovereign contaminant maximum exists for this product form. The four toxic-panel cells and the nickel cell are disclosed read-across values from the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical maximum levels in this row's native basis; the remaining unregulated cells are held under mandatory analytical control with a published method and escalation rule; and the two speciation cells are bounded by their total-element parents. No cell is occurrence-derived.
fabric-protectants.cross_reference: Waterproofing treatments and flame-retardant treatments are outside the Green Seal GS-48 scope that bounds this category and are not certified under this row.
fabric-protectants.audit_exclude_scope: ^toothpaste$|tattooing|permanent make-up|carbon black|colouring agent|colour additive|color additive|modeling clay|clay as a raw material
fabric-protectants.basis_guard: cosmetic product|finished cosmetic as sold|marketed cosmetic product|cosmetic colourant impurity
fabric-protectants.basis_guard_note: Every numeric cell on this row is a disclosed read-across from a sovereign maximum level set on a FINISHED CONSUMER-CHEMICAL PRODUCT expressed as total content of the product as placed on the market. The guard admits only that basis family (80 of the register's 2,993 rows as built) and therefore blocks, at compile time, the four basis conflations that would otherwise be available and would each be indefensible: a dietary wet-weight or as-consumed food maximum level; the EU consumer-textile restriction, which is a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis on the FABRIC rather than a content basis on the product applied to it; article migration and soluble-migration limits (EU Directive 2009/48/EC toys, jewellery and school-article rules); and percent-by-weight deliberate-use article restrictions (EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23 and 47, EU RoHS, and the tattoo and permanent-make-up mixture basis of entry 75). Those instruments are named and dispositioned in the cell substantiations and, where they govern a genuinely related form, are carried as companion limits on the control cells; none of them can anchor a number here.

Pb.basis_label: total lead content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)

read_across.label: disclosed read-across from China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (10 mg/kg lead in a finished consumer-chemical product), the nearest applicable sovereign maximum level on a finished consumer-chemical product in this row's native basis
read_across.substantiation: No sovereign government sets a lead maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product. China GB 14930.1-2022 does not reach this product form and carries no lead row in any event (its grouped heavy-metals line is expressed as combined heavy metals calculated as lead and is not loaded as a lead limit). The sector regimes — Green Seal GS-48 and GS-51 for laundry care products, the EPA Safer Choice programme and its Design for the Environment standard, the EU Ecolabel for detergents and cleaning products (Commission Decisions (EU) 2017/1214 to 2017/1219 and the 2024 user manual, with the JRC 2025 revision in progress), California SB 258 (the Cleaning Product Right to Know Act) and the New York DEC cleansing-product disclosure best-management practice — name lead as a substance of concern for laundry care but set no numeric ceiling, so they establish materiality and supply no number. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; ASEAN, Health Canada and BVL are guidance), and it is already the read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. The Germany BVL 2017 values that the audit scan surfaces as stricter are orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, carried in the register with status 'guidance impurity limit' rather than as statutory maximum levels; Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable MAXIMUM LEVEL set by a credible sovereign government, so a guidance orientation value is not selectable as an anchor. The same reasoning excludes the Health Canada cosmetic impurity limits and the ASEAN, Malaysia and Singapore guidance values. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Lead is measured in this product class in the routed corpus, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. Complete disposition of the stricter rows the compiler's audit safety-net surfaces for this row, none of which is adopted. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, register status 'guidance impurity limit', not statutory maximum levels, and therefore not selectable under Method v2.0. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so the list above is complete and nothing was excluded to make it shorter. Verification method: total lead by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the finish concentrate and, for aerosol and trigger-spray formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. A lot at or above the published ceiling fails; a lot inside the ceiling but outside the running per-row control band is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back.

Cd.basis_label: total cadmium content of the product as placed on the market (consumer-chemical product-content basis; disclosed read-across)

read_across.label: disclosed read-across from China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (5 mg/kg cadmium in a finished consumer-chemical product), the nearest applicable sovereign maximum level on a finished consumer-chemical product in this row's native basis
read_across.substantiation: No sovereign government sets a cadmium maximum for a laundry or fabric-care product. Instruments checked: China GB 14930.1-2022 (the only sovereign detergent contaminant standard in the register; scope is Type A detergents used directly for food cleaning and Type B detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging and containers, and it sets a total-arsenic ceiling only); China NMPA 2015 Safety and Technical Standards for Cosmetics Table 2 (lead, arsenic, mercury, cadmium); Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and its predecessor Notice 2024-9 (lead, cadmium, nickel, antimony, arsenic, mercury); Germany BVL 2017 technically-avoidable heavy metals in cosmetics (lead, cadmium, mercury, arsenic, antimony); Health Canada cosmetic heavy-metal impurity limits; the ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex (2019) and the Malaysia NPRA, Singapore HSA, Indonesia BPOM, Taiwan MoHW and New Zealand cosmetic group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 20 (organotin), entry 23 (cadmium in listed polymers and paints), entry 47 as amended by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (Cr(VI) in skin-contact leather), entry 72 with Appendix 12 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) in consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles) and entry 75 under Regulation (EU) 2020/2081 (tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures); EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy-safety migration limits; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; and the dietary contaminant regimes (EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, Health Canada, UK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V), which are inapplicable both on scope and on basis. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 23 (as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011) restricts cadmium in mixtures and articles produced from listed synthetic organic polymers and in paints, but it is a deliberate-use restriction on cadmium as a pigment and stabiliser in named polymer systems rather than a contaminant maximum for a consumer chemical, and the register row does not enumerate the polymer list, so it is recorded as checked and not adopted rather than read across on an unverified scope. A single coherent sovereign regime is read across per analyte rather than the lowest number picked across regimes, which would build a ceiling no sovereign enforces. China NMPA 2015 Table 2 is the strictest coherent STATUTORY consumer-chemical regime for lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury (Korea MFDS is looser on lead at 20 and on total arsenic at 10 mg/kg; ASEAN, Health Canada and BVL are guidance), and it is already the read-across anchor of the live Category 12 (Household Cleaning and Dishwashing) standard for the identical logical move. Nickel is not regulated by the Chinese instrument at all, so for nickel the nearest applicable sovereign consumer-chemical value is the Korean statutory limit; that is the only regime in the register that sets one, and no number in this row was chosen by comparing outcomes. The Germany BVL 2017 values that the audit scan surfaces as stricter are orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, carried in the register with status 'guidance impurity limit' rather than as statutory maximum levels; Method v2.0 selects the strictest applicable MAXIMUM LEVEL set by a credible sovereign government, so a guidance orientation value is not selectable as an anchor. The same reasoning excludes the Health Canada cosmetic impurity limits and the ASEAN, Malaysia and Singapore guidance values — the Health Canada cosmetic cadmium value of 3 mg/kg that the audit scan surfaces is such a guidance impurity limit, and adopting it for cadmium while lead, arsenic and mercury come from the Chinese instrument would mix regimes for no principled reason. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 with Appendix 12 restricts lead, cadmium, total arsenic and hexavalent chromium to 1 mg/kg in consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear. That instrument governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, and it is expressed on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than on the product-content basis of this category. It is disclosed here as a related but distinct scope and as the downstream constraint a certified product must not cause the treated textile to breach; it is never borrowed as this category's ceiling, and the row's basis_guard makes that borrowing impossible in the compiler. EU REACH Annex XVII entry 75 (Regulation (EU) 2020/2081) sets the strictest sovereign consumer-mixture metal limits in the register (lead 0.7, cadmium 0.5, total arsenic 0.5, mercury 0.5, Cr(VI) 0.5 and nickel 5 mg/kg), but its scope is mixtures for tattooing and permanent make-up, an intradermal-injection route. Reading an injected-mixture ceiling across to a rinse-off or fabric-deposited topical product would conflate exposure routes, and its register basis is a tattoo/permanent-make-up mixture basis that this row's basis_guard excludes. Cadmium is measured in this product class in the routed corpus, so a not-material determination is unavailable on the facts. Complete disposition of the stricter rows the compiler's audit safety-net surfaces for this row, none of which is adopted. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, register status 'guidance impurity limit', not statutory maximum levels, and therefore not selectable under Method v2.0. (2) hc_cosmetic_cd_3ppm (3 mg/kg): a Health Canada cosmetic impurity guidance limit, excluded for the same reason, and adopting it for cadmium alone would additionally mix regimes. (3) eu_2018_1513_pb_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, eu_2018_1513_cd_consumer_textiles_1mgkg and eu_2018_1513_tas_consumer_textiles_1mgkg (1 mg/kg each): the EU consumer-textile restriction, which governs the FABRIC and not the product applied to it, on a homogeneous-material-after-extraction basis rather than this row's product-content basis; carried as a downstream constraint and companion limit, and blocked from anchoring by the row's basis_guard. The audit_exclude_scope on this row removes only the oral/mucosal toothpaste tier, tattoo and permanent-make-up mixtures, and colour-additive and colourant specifications; against the register as built it suppresses no row that the audit scope would otherwise surface, so the list above is complete and nothing was excluded to make it shorter. Verification method: total cadmium by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2, with a hydrofluoric-acid or lithium-metaborate fusion step where an aluminosilicate, silicate or clay mineral phase is present) followed by ICP-MS quantification against matrix-matched calibration standards, with a certified reference material and a reagent blank in every run. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the finish concentrate and, for aerosol and trigger-spray formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. A lot at or above the published ceiling fails; a lot inside the ceiling but outside the running per-row control band is escalated to ALARA review with raw-material trace-back.

not_material.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic and a species of it (iAs <= tAs). No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for a laundry product, a fabric-care product, a detergent or a cosmetic: every consumer-chemical arsenic instrument in the register regulates TOTAL arsenic (China NMPA 2015 Table 2, China GB 14930.1-2022, Korea MFDS Notice 2025-63 and 2024-9, Germany BVL 2017, Health Canada, the ASEAN Annex, and EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12), and no sovereign speciates arsenic for any product in this category. The inorganic fraction is therefore governed by, and bounded by, the total-arsenic ceiling published on the tAs cell of this row. The determination is a governance statement about which cell carries the ceiling, not an assertion that inorganic arsenic is absent, and it is rebuttable: the only routed inorganic-arsenic measurement anywhere in this category's evidence base is zhang2026-cotton-arsenic-amf-calcium, which speciates inorganic arsenic in COTTON FIBRE as a soil-uptake pathway in the textile substrate, not as a contaminant of a product applied to the textile, so it does not rebut this determination for the product itself.
not_material.reference_method: Reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS on the digest of the product as placed on the market, triggered whenever total arsenic exceeds one half of the published total-arsenic ceiling, whenever an arsenic-bearing mineral feedstock is declared, or whenever an agricultural (starch, cellulose or plant-derived surfactant) feedstock is declared. The sampling unit is one composite sample per production lot, drawn from the product as placed on the market, with component-level sampling of the finish concentrate and, for aerosol and trigger-spray formats, the propellant-charged formulation together with the valve and actuator hardware in the product-contact path. Escalation: a speciated inorganic-arsenic result is dispositioned against the total-arsenic ceiling under ALARA with raw-material trace-back to the declared feedstock.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for a laundry, fabric-care, detergent or cosmetic product; every applicable consumer-chemical instrument regulates total arsenic. Inorganic arsenic is a species of and bounded by total arsenic (iAs <= tAs) and is governed through the tAs cell of this row, which carries a published ceiling.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: CN NMPA 2015 cosmetics Table 2; CN GB 14930.1-2022 detergents; KR MFDS Notice 2025-63 and Notice 2024-9; DE BVL 2017; Health Canada cosmetic impurity limits; ASEAN Cosmetic Directive Annex 2019 and the MY NPRA, SG HSA, ID BPOM, TW MoHW and NZ group-standard equivalents; EAEU TR CU 009/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII entries 20, 23, 47, 72 and 75; EU Directive 2009/48/EC toy migration; EU RoHS 2011/65/EU; EU 2023/915, EU 2024/1987, Codex CXS 193, US FDA, FSANZ, UK and HK Cap. 132V (dietary, inapplicable on scope and basis); and the sector regimes Green Seal GS-48/GS-51, EPA Safer Choice/DfE, EU Ecolabel for detergents, California SB 258 and the New York DEC cleansing-product disclosure BMP (no numeric contaminant limits). not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a species of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) formed by microbial methylation in aquatic food webs and concentrated by dietary bioaccumulation in fish muscle. A surfactant, quaternary-ammonium, silicone, starch or mineral laundry formulation has no methylation pathway, no aquatic food-web input and no dietary mercury source, and no routed source in this category's evidence base measures or speciates methylmercury in any product form — the sector standards and the product surveys measure TOTAL mercury. Any mercury present is governed by, and bounded by, the total-mercury ceiling published on the tHg cell of this row. No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for a laundry, fabric-care, detergent or cosmetic product; sovereign methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish and seafood.
not_material.reference_method: Total mercury is the reported screen (dedicated thermal-decomposition amalgamation atomic absorption, or acid digestion with cold-vapour AFS/ICP-MS, on the product as placed on the market). Methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS or LC-ICP-MS is performed only in the event that a total-mercury result approaches the published ceiling and an organomercury source is identified in the formulation.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No sovereign sets a methylmercury maximum level for a laundry, fabric-care, detergent or cosmetic product; methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish and seafood. (1) de_bvl2017_pb_cosmetics_general_2000 (2 mg/kg), de_bvl2017_cd_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1), de_bvl2017_tas_cosmetics_general_500 (0.5) and de_bvl2017_thg_cosmetics_general_100 (0.1): Germany BVL 2017 orientation values for technically avoidable trace content, register status 'guidance impurity limit', not statutory maximum levels, and therefore not selectable under Method v2.0.
